description:
# Goal

Make the 00181 product cache-hit count and trace deterministic across local, coverage, and CI execution without weakening the causal contract or adding retries. Restore a green push boundary before publishing fz-tfn.10.

# Proven failure

CI run 33895141634 on fz-tfn.8 passed all 1,786 library tests, the 525-test serial fixture matrix, 28 other fz2_cli tests, and lint, then failed `the_drain_arbiter_publishes_readiness_only_movement_and_attributes_every_evaluation`. The exact product tuple was `(408, 408, 408, 0, 19, 0)` versus the established `(408, 408, 408, 0, 18, 0)`: only cache hits increased by one. The preceding cross-process target causal/backend reproducibility test passed. This is not the readiness-EOF race in fz-tfn.28 and is not yet proven to be the untriggered producer retry defect in fz-tfn.32.

# Strategy and TDD

1. Reproduce with the smallest exact command and under the coverage/serial ordering used by CI; inspect the one extra ProductCacheHit identity and its preceding request cause.
2. Compare repeated fresh-process traces and the fz-tfn.7 parent to determine whether fz-tfn.8 introduced semantic nondeterminism or the baseline is accidentally order/environment dependent.
3. Fix the structured scheduling/product dependency cause, not the expected count. Do not accept multiple baselines, loosen assertions, add retries/sleeps, or special-case ExecutableEffects.
4. Prove exact product values, generations, settlements, cache-hit identities, causal attribution, backend artifact, and runtime output across repeated processes and coverage.
5. Run focused causal tests, full library, serial fixture matrix, fz2_cli, formatting, strict clippy, and CI.

# Acceptance

Run 33895141634’s failure is reproducible and explained by exact structured product identity. Repeated local and CI coverage executions publish one canonical cache-hit trace/count. All gates are green, and fz-tfn.10 remains unpushed until this ticket is closed and its CI succeeds.
title: Make product cache-hit causality deterministic under coverage
